evidence.claim: Flagged amount $99.92 is well within cardholder historical average of $199.63 (max $1586.94)
Transaction originated from a new unrecognized device profile (Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720)

case.summary: The investigation concludes that transaction 3503878 was a confirmed compromise, not an authorized cardholder spend, and is classified as fraud under the “card_not_present_new_device” pattern. Evidence includes a single $99.92 out‑of‑bounds purchase made from a previously unseen device, with no linked or connected cards and no legitimate customer response to outreach attempts. Accordingly, the card (C07987‑K2) has been blocked for re‑issuance and a fraud case has been created per bank policy.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Customer states they did not recognize the charge and have not shared their card credentials.

initial.reason: R1: Elevated fraud probability on flagged authorization; decline pending inquiry
R1: Require step-up passcode/auth before allowing further activity

final.reason: R2: Customer denied transaction; open case and record to graph

next_best_actions.what_changed: Customer denial confirmed unauthorized transaction, elevating fraud probability to 0.79. Pre-evidence monitoring escalated to immediate BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE under Policy R2. Because exposure ($99.92) is under $1,000 and no cross-card compromise linkage exists, the matter is resolved as case-only without external regulatory SAR filing.

sar.reason: No regulatory filing required under Fraud Policy thresholds (exposure under limit and no multi-account ring link).

stop_reason: Definitive evidence of compromise obtained; protective actions and report executed.
